svg.title: Mike's four caches
svg.text: MIKE'S FOUR CACHES
from the fastest and most fragile to the slowest and most durable
SMALLTALK.PY
PRESTAC.PY
The slot itself (prompt cache)
llama-server keeps the state after the last tokens it read. A request
whose ids start with those tokens reads only the rest.
"cache_prompt": true · lost when the server stops · --cache-ram 0: no second copy
every turn
extend, ask
Frames: the slot saved to a file
/slots/0?action=save writes the state; restore puts it back, with no
token read again. The file grows with the tokens it holds.
--slot-save-path · survives a restart · 0.4–0.5 MB for the chat L0, 13 MB for the tool L0
L0 only
every layer
PreStaC: a stack of frames, prefetched
Store keyed by the hash of the token ids, LRU within 200 MB, atomic commit;
a worker reads the wanted stack in 64-token chunks while the user navigates.
Store · HttpEngine · PreStaC.step / ask · desk prototype only (Step 9.2)
not used
all of it
The operating system's page cache
The 219 MB model file is mapped, not copied. Once read, it stays in RAM while
memory allows. On Luna: first start 11.0 s, the next 8.1 s (both reading L0).
mmap · nobody controls it · after a reboot: slower start, not measured
implicit
implicit
Sources: src/mike/smalltalk.py, src/mike/prestac.py, worklines/mike/docs/0902_01 (frame sizes), 1205_01 (start times on Luna).
